CC-1.analogue: A chain of nine receipts: the root and a leaf eight levels below it.
CC-1.note: No per-receipt depth claim; a chain holds at most 8 receipts in all.

CC-10.analogue: A set replaced by a single-value constraint.
CC-10.note: No single-value type; a one-element array (CC-9) is the equivalent.

CC-11.analogue: A child narrows methods to the empty array.
CC-11.note: The empty set is a subset; the child then matches no request.

CC-12.analogue: A child writes max_body_bytes as 1.0 where its parent wrote 1.
CC-12.note: max_body_bytes must be an integer; 1.0 is malformed.

CC-13.analogue: Pinning an object with a one-element set.
CC-13.note: Grants carry no tool-argument constraints; the draft has no such construct.

CC-14.analogue: Pinning an object with a single-value constraint.
CC-14.note: Grants carry no tool-argument constraints; the draft has no such construct.

CC-2.analogue: A depth limit lowered by a holder.
CC-2.note: No per-receipt depth claim to lower; the fixed chain limit applies to every chain.

CC-3a.analogue: A child names tools where its parent left tools absent (unrestricted).

CC-3b.analogue: The same; there is no partly open tools list to distinguish it from CC-3a.

CC-4a.analogue: A request carries a body where the leaf leaves max_body_bytes absent.
CC-4a.note: An absent member is compared as its default (0).

CC-4b.analogue: A request invokes a tool where the leaf leaves tools absent.

CC-5.analogue: A request that invokes no tool, where the leaf lists tools.
CC-5.note: tools binds only a request that invokes a tool; host, method and path still bind.

CC-6.analogue: A child drops tools its parent listed.

CC-7.analogue: Replacing a bound with one value inside it.
CC-7.note: Each member has one fixed type, so a constraint is never replaced by one of another type.

CC-8.analogue: Pinning a number by tightening both bounds.
CC-8.note: Numeric members are upper bounds only (max_body_bytes, max_calls, max_spend).

CC-9.analogue: A child narrows methods to one element.
